decisions.trade_off: Balancing mechanical durability and impact resistance (to prevent premature structural failure) against the carbon footprint of raw material production and end-of-life recyclability.
decisions.rationale: PCR PC/ABS offers the high impact strength and scratch resistance required for a vacuum cleaner housing (which experiences frequent impacts during use) while reducing the carbon footprint by up to 60% compared to virgin plastics. It also avoids the end-of-life composting/recycling complications associated with bio-based composites in standard municipal waste streams.
decisions.design_action: Verify the supply chain availability and mechanical property consistency of PCR PC/ABS resins from certified suppliers, and check compatibility with standard injection molding draft angles.

options_evaluated: Reversible snap-fits with integrated release points
decisions.trade_off: Permanent assembly (welding) minimizes part count and weight but prevents repair and recycling; metal fasteners facilitate disassembly but increase material complexity; snap-fits allow toolless disassembly but risk fatigue failure during servicing.
decisions.recommendation: Reversible snap-fits with integrated release points for user-accessible areas, combined with standardized metal screws for structural joints
decisions.rationale: This hybrid approach avoids co-molded brass threaded inserts (which contaminate plastic recycling streams) while ensuring that high-wear components (filters, brush rolls) can be accessed toollessly, and the main structural chassis can be fully disassembled at end-of-life using standard workshop tools.
decisions.design_action: Map out the disassembly sequence flow to identify which joints require toolless access versus tool-based access, and verify that the snap-fit geometries do not create molded-in stress concentrations.

decisions.trade_off: Brushed motors are highly recyclable and cheap but have low efficiency and short lifespans; BLDC motors offer extreme efficiency and lifespan but rely on rare-earth magnets with high-impact mining footprints.
decisions.rationale: The operational energy savings and significantly extended product lifespan (due to the absence of brush wear) of a BLDC motor outweigh the upfront environmental impacts of the rare-earth magnets, provided the motor is designed for easy extraction and recycling at end-of-life.
decisions.design_action: Investigate the availability of BLDC motors utilizing recycled neodymium magnets or magnet-free synchronous reluctance technologies, and check supplier specifications for end-of-life reclamation programs.

options_evaluated: Active cooling via dedicated auxiliary fan
Passive cooling via optimized airflow paths using main suction air
Heat pipe integration with aluminum heatsinks
decisions.trade_off: Active cooling adds electronic complexity, weight, and energy consumption; passive suction-cooling reduces energy and parts but risks motor overheating if the suction path or filters become clogged.
decisions.recommendation: Passive cooling via optimized airflow paths using main suction air, supplemented by a thermal cutoff switch
decisions.rationale: Utilizing the existing suction airflow for motor cooling eliminates the need for an auxiliary fan motor, reducing material use, energy consumption, and assembly complexity. The thermal cutoff switch acts as a safety mechanism to prevent catastrophic motor failure during clogs, preserving the product's lifespan.
decisions.design_action: Review historical failure mode data for suction-cooled motors in similar product classes to establish the necessary thermal threshold margins, and verify the spatial envelope required for the thermal cutoff switch.

options_evaluated: Semi-modular architecture with tool-required internal access
decisions.trade_off: High modularity increases the initial material footprint, weight, and electrical connector complexity but drastically extends product life; monolithic designs minimize material use but lead to whole-product disposal upon single-component failure.
decisions.rationale: Vacuum cleaners frequently fail due to localized issues (e.g., battery degradation, motor failure, or brush roll wear). A modular architecture allows users to easily swap out these specific modules without technical expertise, preventing premature disposal of the entire unit and enabling closed-loop recycling of individual modules.
decisions.design_action: Define the boundaries of the modular cartridges and verify that standard, reliable blind-mate connectors can be sourced to link the electrical modules without soldering.

decisions.trade_off: Corded power avoids battery manufacturing impacts and electronic waste but limits usability; cordless batteries offer high convenience but introduce hazardous waste, limited lifespans, and high manufacturing footprints.
decisions.rationale: While corded power is environmentally superior, market demands dictate cordless usability. Utilizing a user-removable battery pack mitigates the environmental downside of cordless design by allowing battery replacement (extending the vacuum's useful life) and enabling the battery to be recycled or used across other household tools.
decisions.design_action: Investigate industry-standard battery pack form factors and communication protocols to determine if an existing battery platform can be adopted, reducing the need for custom battery development.
